naslov: The Group That Will Enter Jannah

segmenti.tekst: جدد حياة القلب بالقرآن كي تطمئن الروح بالإيمان. الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره، ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، أرسله الله بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وسراجا منيرا،

لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين. قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ. أما بعد. Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement, the Lord of jinn and mankind.

May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Respected brothers, honoured believers, our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, informs us in his narrations, in his hadiths, that certain groups,

or certain people, will enter Jannah (Paradise). Why does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, inform us about them? He informs us, dear brothers, because of the beautiful qualities they possess, so that we believers may also adorn ourselves with those qualities.

In a hadith narrated by Iyad, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "وَأَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ ثَلَاثَةٌ" – three will enter Jannah.

What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say? Who is the first who will enter Jannah? The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: in first place, a just ruler, successful, supported by Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Why does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mention the ruler first?
Because, dear brothers, the ruler is the mirror of a people. The ruler is the mirror of a people.
If the ruler is good, then the people too, the people are good. If the ruler is no good, then the people are no good either. Because they are the ones who put him in that position.

Because they are the ones who chose him. We see, dear brothers, what kind of times these are in the world today, and, by Allah, here at home as well. We see for ourselves how many unjust rulers there are.

We see for ourselves what is happening in Gaza, that almost no one comes out… Those are individuals, and they speak about the injustice that is currently taking place. Umar, radiyallahu anhu, said that he feared some animal might injure its leg on the roads he had built.

Imagine, dear brothers. Those rulers cared not only for people, but for animals as well. You know that in the time of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, the fifth rightly guided caliph, they would take food and carry it up into the mountains so that the animals would be fed.

How much do our rulers care for us? How much do our rulers care for the needs of the people? When the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, mentions a ruler here, people, it does not refer only to a ruler, or a president of a state, and so on,
but it refers to everyone who is responsible for a group: whether it be the president of a state, the mayor of a city, a school principal, a mufti, an imam, and so on.
So, if you are just, Allah has promised you Jannah. But the problem is if a person is unjust, oppressing people, oppressing people. What does he say in another hadith?

Three, he says, will enter Jahannam (Hellfire) without being called to account. That is, there will be no question of them being judged. Allah will not judge them at all. In first place, what does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say: the unjust ruler.

That is why, dear brothers, it is very important that the ruler is just – that is, the president of the state, the head of the municipality, the mufti, the imam, every man in the family, the head of the family.

And you see, dear brothers, everything is connected to the family. In the end, everything is connected to the family. Why? Because the family is the pillar of a society. The second man, as the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says, who will enter Jannah – he says: the second man who will enter Jannah is a merciful man, soft-hearted towards every relative.

Here "towards every relative" can be interpreted as towards every Muslim, because we are all, dear brothers, close to one another; we are all brothers. Why precisely such a man, soft-hearted and merciful?

Because the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was merciful. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ الْقَلْبِ لَانْفَضُّوا مِنْ حَوْلِكَ" – and, He says, had you been, O Messenger, harsh and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you. We all know the story of when a Bedouin came to the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, pulled him by the collar and said to him: "Give me money from the state treasury."

It is said that he pulled him so hard that his [unclear] turned red. What does Umar do? He immediately reaches for his sword. The Prophet says: "Easy, Umar. Easy, Umar." The mercy of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. We should adorn ourselves with these qualities, my dear brothers.

Believe me, a person should not get angry with his brother over some trifle, if the man does not greet him in the street. Sometimes, dear brothers, a person has so many worries. Believe me, you look at him, the man walks down the street staring at one point.

He sees neither me, nor you, nor anyone. Because debts, worries and so on are weighing on him. That is why a person should look for an excuse for his Muslim brother. He should be "rahimul-qalb," merciful, and not get angry with his brother over some little trifle, or some small thing, or something he did not understand at that moment; rather, we should look for excuses for our brothers.
And those most deserving of our mercy, dear brothers, are our parents, dear brothers, our parents.

You see for yourselves what kind of times these are, that we have people who beat their parents. How can you expect such a person to be merciful tomorrow towards you, towards me, and so on? If a person… if a person insults his neighbour, his brother, and so on,

how can you expect him to be merciful? That is why we need to change. That is why the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, tells us about these qualities, so that we may adorn ourselves with them. And the last thing that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam… that is, the last man of these three who will enter Jannah, the one he mentions last to us, is, as he says, a chaste man. A chaste, honest man, a family man, who does not have much money.

But what is his quality? He does not ask of others. He does not ask of others. He is in need, in great need, but he does not hold out his hand for someone to help him; instead he works and strives for his family, in order to provide for his family.

In order to provide for his family. And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has promised him Jannah. And you know, dear brothers, when a child comes – such are the times now – a child comes home having seen something there at school.

Someone has something, some child has something that his father bought him, his own father. And then he comes to him: "Dad, buy me one," and so on. Believe me, it is hard to restrain oneself and be one of these people and not ask.

And that is why Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, made the promise. Why? So that a person relies on Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. So that a person relies on Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, that he works – of course, that he works and strives – and then relies on Allah, and Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will give him provision. "وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا" – and whoever fears Allah, Allah will make a way out for him.

These are these, these three men who will enter Jannah. They are not the only ones, but the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, tells us about them in certain hadiths, that is, about certain groups, precisely, precisely because of that importance, or these qualities they have, so that we too may adorn ourselves with these qualities and be, in sha Allah, among them. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to forgive our sins and the sins of our parents. I ask Him, the Exalted, to help us here in the Sandžak. I ask Him, the Exalted, to help our brothers

in Gaza. I ask Him, the Exalted, to help them against the unbelievers, against those [unclear]. I ask Him, the Exalted, to bring us together in Jannah. Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin. Aqulu qawli hadha wa astaghfirullaha li wa lakum, fastaghfiruhu, innahu huwal-Ghafurur-Rahim.
